card.name: Ancient texts and sages' names
card.fires_on: Inside or right after names of ancient sages, classic texts and Talmudic or Chinese sources (Rashi, Mencius, Shen Nung, Menachos), and in phrases about ancient history. It fires on the name's ending or the next small word.

modes.label: Jewish sources
modes.description: Partway through names of rabbis, Talmud tractates or biblical books.

modes.label: Chinese classics
modes.description: On the ending of ancient Chinese figures or texts such as Mencius and Nei Ching.
modes.example: Zhang Pengwei, Guo Qiyong & Wang Bei (2008). New Insight Into Mencius<<'>> Theory of the Original Goodness in Human

modes.label: Ancient history phrasing
modes.description: On small words in statements about how old something is.
modes.example: malaria has cursed human history for more<< than>> 4,000 years.

card.writes: It suppresses words meaning ancient, so it seems to steer away from repeating 'ancient' when the text is already about old sources.
card.plain: It lights up in text about ancient sages and old classic books, especially Jewish and Chinese ones.
